## 2b7bcfbf942b

**Reproduced defect — severe canonical-profile collapse and shortcut exposure.**

Canonical inputs contain either one or two objects and cover bounding-box profiles `5×5`, `6×4 + 6×4`, `6×6`, `5×5 + 6×4`, and `6×7`. In 120 deterministic generated draws across all three bands, every input had exactly two objects and both were exactly `3×4`. A learner can therefore memorize two fixed-size templates/locations instead of learning the general per-object bounding-box checker-fill transformation represented by the canonical set.

The same probe found four declared controls—`anchor_corner`, `asymmetry_force`, `palette_kind`, and `position_bias`—to be inert for the tested paired overrides, and `self_check([[1,2]])` returned no error. These measurements reinforce that the generator's declared/validated manifold is much broader on paper but much narrower in actual output.

A minimal concrete counterexample to generated support is canonical pair 0: one `5×5` object. The sampled generator never produced any one-object input or any `5×5` bounding box. Probe: `repo/generators/3108da8bf9e8/workspace/audit_probe.py`; retained output: `checks/audit-probe-console.log`.

triage.reason: Read and retained with later revision; original notes, audits and solve records preserved.
